purpose: Measurement-science primer injected into the student's prompt (retrieval-style knowledge, not fine-tuning). Sources: AIMS competition page and baseline repo; Lord (1980) IRT; Murphy (1973) Brier decomposition; organizers' ECE definition.

concepts.name: Item response theory (1PL/2PL)
concepts.formula: P(y=1 | theta_s, b_i) = sigmoid(theta_s - b_i)  (1PL);  2PL: sigmoid(a_i (theta_s - b_i))
concepts.meaning: theta_s = subject ability, b_i = item difficulty, a_i = discrimination. Effects are additive on the LOGIT scale, not on the probability scale. A subject's ability is shared across items; an item's difficulty is shared across subjects.
concepts.use_in_this_predictor: slot IRT_ENVELOPE and the v402 estimator; the zero-shot ease d_i is a stand-in for -b_i.

concepts.name: Conjugate Beta-Binomial shrinkage
concepts.formula: E[theta | S, N] = (S + a) / (N + a + b)
concepts.meaning: a and b are pseudo-counts: prior strength in units of observations. Larger a+b = slower reaction to new labels. The three mixture regimes are three such priors with weights updated by the likelihood.

concepts.name: Brier score and Murphy decomposition
concepts.meaning: reliability (calibration error, lower is better) = how far predicted probabilities are from observed frequencies; resolution (higher is better) = how much predictions separate outcomes; uncertainty = ybar(1-ybar), fixed by the data. A constant prediction equal to the pass rate has zero reliability error and zero resolution, i.e. Brier = uncertainty.
concepts.use_in_this_predictor: the oracle-constant floor is Brier = uncertainty; any gain below it must come from resolution (item-level discrimination).

concepts.name: Expected calibration error (organizers' definition)
concepts.formula: ECE = sum_k (n_k / N) |mean_pred_k - mean_y_k| over 10 equal-width probability bins, weighted by response count
concepts.meaning: diagnostic only; sensitive to sample size. Changes that only rescale probabilities move ECE but may not move Brier.

concepts.name: Learning curve and ALC
concepts.meaning: budgets 1 and 3 carry 40% of the weight; a change that only helps at 31 labels is worth at most 0.1 of its Brier effect.
concepts.use_in_this_predictor: prefer slots that act at budgets 1-7.

concepts.name: Leave-one-benchmark-out validation
concepts.formula: for each benchmark b: fit on all others, score on b; report paired differences on identical pairs
concepts.meaning: the only evidence the gate accepts; hosted formative scores come from different samples per submission and cannot rank candidates.

concepts.name: Reliability across trials
concepts.formula: trial agreement = fraction of items whose repeated attempts give the same outcome
concepts.meaning: 76-100% on the public benchmarks; only matharena and agentdojo have meaningful repeat noise. Predictions near 0 or 1 are therefore not unreasonable on deterministic benchmarks but dangerous where repeats disagree.
concepts.use_in_this_predictor: output clipping bounds and the mixture regimes.

rules_for_proposals: Propose changes that act at budgets 1-7 before changes that act only at 31.
When a slot's proposals so far are indistinguishable from the baseline, move to the ends of the allowed ranges.
Never justify a baseline by a single hosted score; justify it by LOBO paired evidence.
Additive effects belong on the logit scale; if a proposal adds to probabilities, say so in the hypothesis.
